# Accessibility

Bound by the UCSD Accessibility Standards, ADA Title II, and WCAG 2.1 AA. All
generated content must be usable by people with disabilities.

## Layout and structure

- Use semantic HTML5 elements (`<header>`, `<nav>`, `<main>`, `<article>`,
  `<footer>`, `<aside>`) rather than generic `<div>` and `<span>` wrappers.
- Exactly one `<h1>` per page. Heading levels descend without skipping.
- `tabindex` is only ever `0` or `-1`. Never a positive value.
- Interactive elements keep a visible keyboard focus state.
- Never use the `title` attribute for tooltips — it is unavailable to mobile and
  to most keyboard users.
- Never disable viewport zoom.

## Interactive elements

- Everything operable by mouse is operable by Tab and Shift+Tab.
- Touch targets are at least 44×44 px.
- Every interactive element has an accessible name. If there is no visible text,
  add `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby`.
- `target="_blank"` requires text saying so — "(opens in new window)".

## Forms

- Bind every input to a `<label>` with `for`/`id`. A visually hidden label uses
  `.sr-only`; it is not omitted.
- Render validation errors above the form so screen readers reach them after a
  failed submission.
- Use standard `autocomplete` values for known fields (`name`, `tel`,
  `street-address`, `email`).
- Avoid `autofocus`. It disorients screen reader users on page load. The pristine
  Decorator search markup ships with it — remove it.

## Content and presentation

- Minimum 3:1 contrast against adjacent colors for UI components, graphical
  objects, and text.
- Never use color as the only means of conveying information or state.
- Every `<img>` has a meaningful `alt`, or `alt=""` if genuinely decorative.
- No strobe or flashing. Nothing flashes more than three times per second.

## Assistive technology

- A full page starts with a skip link to `<main>`.
- Use ARIA to supplement native semantics, never to contradict them. Do not put
  `role="button"` on a `<button>`.
- Keep `aria-expanded`, `aria-controls`, and `aria-hidden` in sync with actual
  state.

## Standards

- <https://accessibility.ucsd.edu/checklists/websites.html>
- <https://accessibility.ucsd.edu/policies-standards/ucsd-accessibility-guidelines.html>
- <https://www.w3.org/TR/WCAG21/>

Automated checks do not replace manual verification. Confirm keyboard order,
focus visibility, zoom and reflow at 200%, and screen reader output for any
component you add or change.
